{{technical|date=September 2026}}
{{Short description|Characteristic subgroup of a profinite group}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=September 2026}}

In [[mathematics]], the '''Melnikov group''' or '''Melnikov subgroup''' of a [[profinite group]] <math>G</math>, denoted <math>M(G)</math>, is the intersection of all maximal open [[normal subgroup]]s of <math>G</math>.{{sfn|Fried|Jarden|2023|pp=637–638}}{{sfn|Klopsch|Quick|2023|p=152}} If <math>G</math> is nontrivial, then <math>M(G)</math> is a proper closed subgroup invariant under every continuous automorphism of <math>G</math> (that is, it is topologically [[characteristic subgroup|characteristic]]).{{sfn|Klopsch|Quick|2023|p=152}} Fried and Jarden use the term "Melnikov group", while later literature also uses "Melnikov subgroup".{{sfn|Fried|Jarden|2023|p=637}}{{sfn|Klopsch|Quick|2023|p=152}}

The construction is a normal-subgroup analogue of the [[Frattini subgroup]] <math>\Phi(G)</math>. Whereas the Frattini subgroup is defined using all maximal open subgroups, the Melnikov group uses only maximal open ''normal'' subgroups.{{sfn|Fried|Jarden|2023|pp=637–638}} Equivalently, <math>M(G)</math> is the intersection of the kernels of all continuous epimorphisms from <math>G</math> onto finite [[simple group]]s. It therefore records the part of <math>G</math> that is invisible in every finite simple quotient.{{sfn|Fried|Jarden|2023|pp=637–638}}

== Definition and simple quotients ==
Throughout, homomorphisms of profinite groups are understood to be continuous. A proper open normal subgroup <math>N</math> of <math>G</math> is '''maximal open normal''' if there is no proper open normal subgroup of <math>G</math> strictly between <math>N</math> and <math>G</math>. The Melnikov group is

:<math>M(G)=\bigcap\{N\trianglelefteq G:N\text{ is maximal open normal in }G\}.</math>{{sfn|Fried|Jarden|2023|p=637}}

If <math>N</math> is maximal open normal, then <math>G/N</math> is a finite simple group. Conversely, if <math>S</math> is a finite simple group and <math>\varphi:G\twoheadrightarrow S</math> is an epimorphism, then <math>\ker\varphi</math> is maximal open normal. Thus

:<math>M(G)=\bigcap\{\ker\varphi:\varphi:G\twoheadrightarrow S,\; S\text{ is a finite simple group}\}.</math>{{sfn|Fried|Jarden|2023|p=637}}

For a finite simple group <math>S</math>, define

:<math>M_S(G)=\bigcap\{N\trianglelefteq G:G/N\cong S\},</math>

with <math>M_S(G)=G</math> when <math>G</math> has no quotient isomorphic to <math>S</math>. Then

:<math>M(G)=\bigcap_S M_S(G).</math>

For each <math>S</math>, the quotient <math>G/M_S(G)</math> is a [[Direct product of groups|Cartesian power]] of <math>S</math>. More precisely,

:<math>G/M(G)\cong\prod_S S^{r_G(S)},</math>

where <math>S</math> ranges over the isomorphism classes of finite simple groups and <math>r_G(S)</math> is the <math>S</math>-rank of <math>G</math>, equivalently the cardinal number of copies of <math>S</math> occurring in <math>G/M_S(G)</math>.{{sfn|Fried|Jarden|2023|pp=637–638}}{{sfn|Fried|Jarden|2023|pp=644–646}} In particular,

:<math>M(G)=1</math> if and only if <math>G</math> is a Cartesian product of finite simple groups.{{sfn|Fried|Jarden|2023|p=637}}

This also characterizes <math>G/M(G)</math> as the largest quotient of <math>G</math> that is a Cartesian product of finite simple groups: every homomorphism from <math>G</math> onto such a product factors through <math>G/M(G)</math>.{{sfn|Fried|Jarden|2023|pp=637–638}}

== Basic properties ==
The Melnikov group has several useful functorial and normal-generation properties. Let <math>G</math> and <math>H</math> be profinite groups.{{sfn|Fried|Jarden|2023|pp=637–638}}

* If <math>\alpha:G\twoheadrightarrow H</math> is an epimorphism, then <math>\alpha(M(G))=M(H)</math>.
* If <math>N</math> is a closed normal subgroup of <math>G</math>, then <math>M(N)\leq M(G)</math>.
* If <math>N</math> is a closed normal subgroup of <math>G</math> and <math>NM(G)=G</math>, then <math>N=G</math>.

The last property expresses the role of <math>M(G)</math> in normal generation: adjoining <math>M(G)</math> to a proper closed normal subgroup cannot make it equal to the whole group.{{sfn|Fried|Jarden|2023|p=637}}

== Relation with the Frattini subgroup ==
For every profinite group <math>G</math>, the [[Frattini subgroup]] is contained in the Melnikov group:

:<math>\Phi(G)\leq M(G).</math>{{sfn|Fried|Jarden|2023|p=637}}

The containment can be strict. For the [[symmetric group]] <math>S_3</math>, viewed as a finite profinite group, the only maximal proper normal subgroup is <math>A_3</math>, so

:<math>M(S_3)=A_3,</math>

whereas <math>\Phi(S_3)=1</math>.{{sfn|Fried|Jarden|2023|p=637}}

For [[pro-p group|pro-<math>p</math> groups]], however, the two constructions agree. Every maximal open subgroup of a pro-<math>p</math> group is normal and has index <math>p</math>, and consequently

:<math>M(G)=\Phi(G)</math>

for every pro-<math>p</math> group <math>G</math>.{{sfn|Fried|Jarden|2023|p=637}}

== Melnikov covers ==
An epimorphism <math>\alpha:G\twoheadrightarrow H</math> of profinite groups is called a '''Melnikov cover''' if

:<math>\ker\alpha\leq M(G).</math>{{sfn|Fried|Jarden|2023|p=638}}

This condition has a normal-generation interpretation: <math>\alpha</math> is a Melnikov cover if and only if every closed normal subgroup <math>N\trianglelefteq G</math> satisfying <math>\alpha(N)=H</math> is equal to <math>G</math>. Melnikov covers are closed under composition. Moreover, a Melnikov cover induces an isomorphism

:<math>G/M(G)\;\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }\;H/M(H).</math>{{sfn|Fried|Jarden|2023|p=638}}

Thus a Melnikov cover preserves the quotient obtained after factoring out the Melnikov subgroup.

== Uses ==
The Melnikov subgroup occurs in constructions that separate abelian and simple quotients of profinite groups. Bary-Soroker, Fehm and Wiese define a generalized derived subgroup <math>D(G)</math> satisfying

:<math>D(G)=M(G)\cap G',</math>

where <math>G'</math> is the [[commutator subgroup]]. Iterating this operation gives their ''abelian-simple length'', which they use in criteria for the preservation of the [[Hilbertian field|Hilbertian]] property in algebraic extensions.{{sfn|Bary-Soroker|Fehm|Wiese|2016|pp=125–127}}

Also, this subgroup appears in modern structure theory for profinite groups{{sfn|Klopsch|Quick|2023|pp=149–152}}
